findings.MAJOR-1: R-01.2 decay clock (t0 in year-ticks, rem0 in millionths, lifeYt) replaces the per-day rateMilli; failYt and every event instant in closed form with an exact inverse; HP byte derived, never the schedule; recomputed R-01.6, R-02.4, R-09.3 (FX-R-01 instants in yt); AT-R-01, AT-R-20, MR-15, MR-16
findings.MINOR-1: R-07.3 visitor years now cite FX-R-01 H1 at wR 50 (R-09.3), counted from abandonment at y11
findings.MINOR-2: R-08.5 keys every record by instant dueYt; short heap drained every tick for remains and FOOD; long heap day-drained on purpose with the whole-year checkpoint identity; AT-R-08 sub-day placement
findings.MINOR-3: header Limits row and R-05 intro: sibling tips re-sampled; Lane Q section 9.7 cited as the reconciliation record (Lane Q owns it); R-05 stays PARTIAL
findings.MINOR-4: R-01.2 rebase rule (rem0 <- rem(t1), t0 <- t1, lifeYt <- new life, heap entry replaced; t1 = causing instant) and R-05.4 step 3

requirements.notes: Lives authored in simulated years (D-1 neutral) and turned into one decay clock per record (Fix 1, R-01.2): t0 in year-ticks (1/2,400 sy, exactly DPY ticks), rem0 in millionths of life, lifeYt. Closed forms rem(t), cross(p) and failYt are integer with an exact inverse; the HP byte is derived and written only at thresholds, so lives far longer than 1,000 x maxHP game days fit (u32 lifeYt, about 1.79 million sy). ADR-003 L1653 per-day rateMilli is not used (it cannot hold ASHLAR SHELTERED 20,000 sy and disagrees between DPY 1 and 20); proposed as an ADR-003 amendment. Rebase rule on an exposure or modifier change at the causing instant. 17 decay classes scaled by weatherResistance, rotResistance, corrosionResistance; 7 exposure classes; freeze-thaw, snow, roots and fire modifiers in eighths; default lives with sources; maintenance, abandonment grace, site abandonment. WET depends on D-4. Decay ignoring the SRD damage threshold is OQ-R-09.

Stages S0 intact to S7 rock with entry rules on the life fraction h = rem / R (exact transition instants), strata/object representation, ledger entries and catalogue slot names (names only, DEC-011); decay members share one clock and are split and rebased when exposure or HP diverges; walls in 2-slice bands so they lose height from the top; roofs before walls with a data validator; shedding, rot of organic rubble, pedogenesis; per-material chains (ASHLAR row recomputed in Fix 1). Needs LAND-5 (buildings as built strata) and new strata materials (Lane Q). S7 lithification is specified but Owner-gated (OQ-R-03).

Unattended-item weathering with composite components and a decay clock per item; organic rot to SOIL-ORG plus an AIR sink (the missing soil-nutrient field, DEC-3); remains for every death with stages on one clock, sub-day stages (0.25 sy corpse, FOOD 0.05-0.1 sy) as exact instants drained every tick (Fix 1); bone to soil; anchors kept 200 sy for SRD resurrection windows; metals corrode to OXIDE in steps at clock crossings, four-rule ore guard; SRD rust monster, oozes, mending, creation, gentle repose (a clock pause) mapped; relics and buried finds (ITEM-BURIED). Lane W's design, merged (bed949e8, main 8997e238), assumes its own hand-off (IA-R1); names and mass unit are reconciled under PROPOSED-R-04 and Lane Q's escalation. Conflicts with DURABILITY.md:320, REMAINS.md and PEOPLES.md are OQ-R-04 and OQ-R-06; special materials OQ-R-05.

One residue.burn function called by SIM.50.05: ash and charcoal by class and burn completeness, gas to a named AIR sink by remainder (exact); bone calcines; metals survive; residue to per-cell records and ASH strata at one slice of mass; weathering of ash to soil and charcoal to soil carbon; buried horizons permanent (TR-7); charcoal never becomes coal. Whether exposed ash beds are permanent (WG.63.04 wording) is OQ-R-07.

Ownership split and a contract with Lane Q: HP writes only at Lane Q's capacity thresholds (at exact cross instants); decay never removes matter, it calls Lane Q's single break path; collapse events carry the causing instant atYt and drive local exposure recomputation and rebases at that instant; an instant barrier keeps decay chains DPY- and LOD-independent (Fix 1); bounded work of 64 cells per event. PARTIAL: written against the Lane Q brief (9103799e); Fix 1 re-sampled the tips (Lane Q design at 9d5b40d3, Grok FAIL, in its own Fix 1; the tip moves) and cites Lane Q section 9.7 as the reconciliation record, which is Lane Q's. Names stay ASSUMED; atYt, the clock and the barrier are new items for that reconciliation. Props under natural rock depend on DEC-010 (OPEN).

New reclamation rule overturning DEUS_Objects.js:266 (never on maintained built cells, by stage on abandoned ones); spread from neighbours only; root feedback; burial by own rubble, mudbrick melt and shedding, litter to soil per footprint in closed form, and SIM.50.03 sediment; underground variants per band (-1, Lower-1, Lower-2) with cave fungus, flooding (D-4 dependency) and lava; upper layers shed their ruins downward via Lane Q's cascade.

Site state machine ACTIVE, DECLINING, ABANDONED, RUIN (sets isRuined, the X-7 fix), MOUND, REFOUNDED; eight named trace-retention rules TR-1..TR-8 with minimum retention times and the only processes that remove them; visitor table from FX-R-01 H1 at wR 50 counted from abandonment (Fix 1 corrected the citation); salvage by mass with a worked example (closes LAND-1 for this path); re-founding on foundations using only missing slices (SET-4). Retention times are OQ-R-02; who may re-found whose ruins is OQ-R-08 and depends on D-6.

Decay is per record and closed form, so the same heaps serve L0, L1, L2 and day jumps (ADR-003 L1693, L1696); decay-caused exposure changes rebase at the causing instant, so decay chains are LOD-invariant (Fix 1); every record keyed by instant dueYt; long heap drained at day boundaries on purpose, short heap (remains, FOOD) drained every tick for sub-day lives; whole-year checkpoints are DPY-independent (ceilDiv identity). Cohort records only for records-less matter with largest-remainder promotion; day-jump cost worked example; calendar mapping for D-1 options (a) and (b) without choosing, plus SRD day-versus-year limits. Aged-world starts are ADR-003 Q6 against INV-SIM-01 and are not answered here.

Fixture FX-R-01 (abandoned hamlet: stone, mudbrick, burned timber and brick-tower structures, roads, a cellar at -1, a cave shrine at -3, items, remains; elm timber; deterministic vegetation stand-in; whole-year scripted events) aged to y12,000 at 9 and 32 layers and at DPY 1 and 20; assertions A1-A9 (exact classes, closure, zero ore delta, trace retention, oracle stages and instants, determinism including DPY, LOD invariance, work bound, save/load); exact S1-S4 and band-failure instants in year-ticks from R-01.2 (Fix 1), S5 approximate; stated assumptions (roofs fail at HP 0, band rubble spills to the foot); mutants MR-01..MR-16 including the per-day rateMilli schedule (MR-15) and a rebase at the processing day (MR-16); optional 1,000,000-sy lithification run.

Typed layouts with byte counts for members (clock fields t0 f64, rem0 u32, lifeYt u32 replace hp0, d0, rateMilli, nextDay: still 40 B), structures (32 B), sites (16 B), 12-B heap entries in two heaps, item clocks (20 B), remains (36 B), residue entries (density-adaptive per chunk) with 16-B clock blocks while weathering, cohorts; per-site, per-region and per-layer memory (no layer-count term); scenario Y0 (about 113 KB) and an assumed scenario L (about 23-25 MB) with arithmetic; CPU per tick under both D-1 options; save representation (maintained members rebuilt; lifeYt saved; caches never saved), scenario L about 10.9 MB.

AT-R-01..AT-R-22 mapped to SIM.40.05-.09 and the SIM.40.02, SIM.40.10, SIM.50.05, SIM.50.09 and SIM.60.03 interfaces; each names its fixture, assertion and a mutant that must fail; all run at 9 and 32 layers. Fix 1: AT-R-01 checks the closed form, a 20,000-sy life and the rebase; AT-R-08 checks sub-day placement; AT-R-20 compares instants and checkpoint states at DPY 1 and 20 with the per-day-rate and processing-day mutants.

Placement in the audit's section 6 order; PROPOSED-R-01..R-12 with real dependency IDs and acceptance tests; recommended dependency additions for SIM.40.05, .07, .08 and SIM.50.05; three proposed ADR-003 section 17 amendments (clock for L1653, causing instant for L1694, short heap for L1689-1690); overlaps with WG.65.x and WG.61.02; stale geometry in WG.65.02, SIM.30.01, INV-GEO-01/02; a table of flagged disagreements including ADR-003 vs Fix 1, Lane Q's C2 and Lane W's IA-R1; D-4, D-6, DEC-010 and D-1 dependencies. Owner questions are in the section '## Owner questions'.

proposedPackages.title: Decay parameter data (decay classes, exposure classes, lives, thresholds, residue fractions) and its validator
acceptanceTests: AT-R-02: validator exits 1 on any life <= 0, any disallowed infinity, any finite life whose lifeYears x 2,400 is not an integer or whose lifeYt exceeds 2^32 - 2, any ore/coal/gem/fossil output, or any structure template whose ROOF life at SKY is not shorter than its WALL life at SHELTERED; mutant with ROOF and WALL lives swapped must fail

AT-R-20: FX-R-01 at DPY 1 and DPY 20 gives identical transition instants (year-ticks) and identical stages and ledger totals at every whole-year checkpoint; mutants that must fail: one duration authored in days instead of simulated years, the per-day rateMilli schedule (MR-15), a rebase at the processing day (MR-16)

proposedPackages.title: Decay members, the decay clock (R-01.2) and the instant-keyed scheduler with long and short heaps (R-08.5)
acceptanceTests: AT-R-01: rem and the derived HP byte equal the R-01.2 closed form at sampled instants; events land on their cross instants; a 20,000-sy member fails at exactly 48,000,000 yt at DPY 1 and 20; a rebase sets rem0 = rem(t1), t0 = t1 and the new lifeYt; HP bytes written only at published thresholds and at failure; mutants that must fail: HP written every day, the per-day rateMilli schedule (fails at 6,000 sy at DPY 20), a rebase that keeps the old t0

AT-R-05: at the roof failDay Lane Q's break path is called once per roof member, wall tops become SKY, at most 64 cells enqueued per event; mutant that turns strata to air inside decay must fail (ledger leak, no collapse event)
AT-R-18: decay heap and record bytes identical at 9 and 32 layers on the sparse fixture; mutant with a per-layer dense residue plane must fail
AT-R-19: save at y1,000, reload, continue gives identical checksums; mutant that does not rebuild the heap on load must fail

proposedPackages.title: Maintenance, upkeep coverage, abandonment and the site state machine (X-7 isRuined fix)
acceptanceTests: AT-R-03: a maintained site has zero decay heap entries and zero decay work over 10 game days; mutant that ignores maintenance must fail
AT-R-04: population to 0 gives ABANDONED after siteAbandonYears and RUIN with isRuined true at S3 on half the mass, and History's reader sees site.ruined; mutant that never sets isRuined must fail

proposedPackages.title: Item weathering, remains to soil, and buried finds; reconcile the remains hand-off names and mass unit with Lane W (IA-R1)
acceptanceTests: AT-R-07: an unattended iron longsword corrodes in 4 steps and its grip rots, masses exact; the same sword carried never changes; mutant in which attended items decay must fail

AT-R-08: an off-screen death makes a remains record whose mass goes to SOIL-ORG, SOIL-MIN and AIR exactly, anchor kept 200 sy, gentle repose pauses the clock 10 game days; at DPY 1 a SKY death at tick k becomes SKELETAL on tick k + 600 and a loaf rots on tick k + 240; mutants that must fail: remains removed after 12 game hours, remains and food drained only at day boundaries
AT-R-11: covering an item or member reclassifies it as buried in the same tick and excavation re-exposes it; mutant with no burial reclassification must fail

proposedPackages.title: Corrosion to OXIDE trace minerals and the ore guard
acceptanceTests: AT-R-06: static transform-table check plus runtime guard rejects and logs any ore write with a non-generation cause; no recipe accepts OXIDE; mutant in which corrosion outputs ore must fail

AT-R-21: five rust-monster hits destroy a weapon and move its iron to OXIDE exactly; the antennae destroy 7,840 mu of an unattended iron object; mutant keeping conjured residue as permanent charcoal must fail

proposedPackages.title: Fire residue function: ash, charcoal and the carbon AIR sink (closes FIR-3)
acceptanceTests: AT-R-09: burning timber, cloth, iron nails, a lead cup and bone gives exact ash, charcoal, gas and SCRAP masses and keeps the metals; mutant deleting items on a burned cell must fail; mutant computing gas with floor instead of the remainder must fail

proposedPackages.title: Reclamation rule and burial exposure, surface and underground
acceptanceTests: AT-R-10: plants establish on an abandoned S3 floor and never on a maintained built cell; mutant keeping the DEUS_Objects.js:266 guard must fail; mutant removing the guard entirely must fail

AT-R-12: members at layers -3 and -12 never get SKY or FT above 0, cave fungus halves timber lives, a flood makes members WET; mutant with the bottom layer hard-coded at -2 or -4 must fail at 32 layers

proposedPackages.title: Trace retention, salvage by mass and re-founding on foundations

AT-R-14: re-founding on H1 consumes items only for missing slices and reused slices keep their mass; mutant in which ruin cells block building must fail

proposedPackages.title: Deep-history day jumps and cohort decay for records-less matter

AT-R-16: aging FX-R-01 by 10,000 sy processes no more heap events than the oracle count and none in maintained periods; mutant evaluating every member every year must fail the event bound

proposedPackages.title: Long-run matter ledger fixture FX-R-01 (SIM.40.09)
acceptanceTests: AT-R-17: FX-R-01 aged to y12,000 at 9 and 32 layers and at DPY 1 and 20 satisfies A1-A9 at every checkpoint, with member-failure and stage instants equal to the oracle (R-09.3 table); each of mutants MR-01..MR-16 (leaks, ore creation, foundation and relic erasure, vanishing remains, fire deleting items, double yield, nondeterminism, full scan, stale geometry, lost heap, walls before roofs, coal from charcoal, per-day rateMilli schedule, rebase at the processing day) must fail

proposedPackages.title: Reconcile design documents (REMAINS, PEOPLES, DURABILITY, WORLD_ARCHITECTURE) and stale invariants with this design (docs only, Coordinator)

ownerQuestions.question: How fast should decay run? (interacts with D-1; see the mapping table in 'Deep history and LOD')
options: (a) the real-world-order default lives in the design (a timber roof in 60 simulated years, stone walls in millennia)
(b) all lives divided by one factor (for example 10) so ruins form within a play session
(c) separate factors for structures and for items and remains

ownerQuestions.question: How long must ruins stay recognisable (LIFE-003)?
options: (a) foundations, vaults and mounds indefinitely unless a physical process removes them (the TR-1..TR-8 default)
(b) at least 10,000 simulated years, after which natural erosion may erase them
(c) at least 1,000 simulated years

ownerQuestions.question: Is lithification (buried sediment becoming rock) in scope?
options: (a) no: the cycle ends at consolidated sediment and soil strata (ADR-003 L1680)
(b) only in deep-history day jumps, never in live play
(c) yes, live, under the ore guard

ownerQuestions.question: Do unattended items weather, given 'Items have no HP ... Tools don't wear out' (docs/design/DURABILITY.md:320) and SIM.40.07 / V138?
options: (a) unattended items weather through a condition field (not HP); tools in use never wear
(b) only organic items rot; metal never corrodes
(c) no item weathering (SIM.40.07 would need rewording)

ownerQuestions.question: Do mithral, adamantine and magic items decay?
options: (a) never
(b) very slowly
(c) per-item data

ownerQuestions.question: Which remains timings apply (REMAINS.md:175 and PEOPLES.md:215 disagree), and how long is a dead person's identity anchor kept?
options: (a) physical durations in simulated years (skeleton in 0.25 sy in the open) with the anchor kept at least 200 sy for true resurrection
(b) REMAINS.md's game-hour durations as the look, with the physical clock underneath
(c) PEOPLES.md's 30 and 120 days

ownerQuestions.question: Are ash beds permanent when exposed (WG.63.04, SIM.50.05 'permanent ash beds')?
options: (a) buried ash beds are permanent; exposed ash weathers to soil in about 5 simulated years
(b) exposed ash beds never weather
(c) the ash look stays while its mass goes to soil

ownerQuestions.question: Who may re-found whose ruins?
options: (a) any culture on any ruin
(b) only the same race or culture
(c) per race in the DEC-015 plan data (depends on D-6)

ownerQuestions.question: Does decay lower HP past an object's SRD damage threshold (game/data/srd51/rules.json:7167)?
options: (a) yes, decay ignores the damage threshold
(b) objects with a threshold decay at a reduced rate
(c) they never decay
